items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: And you know Michael Brecker, he’s a friend of mine, he said the same thing.

ctx.x: Yeah, their investment. I mean it’s obvious to anybody whose — and that’s a good thing because I think it makes us more independent. You know I think the music will be stronger, it should actually be more adventuresome, it should be different. I thought what happened in sort of like in the late nineties or in the early eighties was — I’m sure that you found this to be the same thing — there were so many CDs that were coming out where they were all the same format, very few people were trying to do different…
Why is that? © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
